title: Weighted admission controller and graceful degradation playbook for multi-region overloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a Weighted Admission Controller (WAC) and an associated graceful degradation playbook to protect SLOs during multi-region capacity pressure and partial outage scenarios. WAC combines tenant- and region-aware token-bucket admission, priority queues for critical lanes, and configurable degradation strategies (response trimming, model fallbacks, feature gating) to keep overall latency and availability SLOs within targets while minimizing customer impact.
background: Recent multi-region incidents showed that our current shedding mechanisms are either too coarse (global circuit breakers) or too aggressive (drop first-in sessions). We need a targeted, workload-aware approach that: 1) respects contractual SLAs for reserved/dedicated customers, 2) limits noisy-tenant impact, and 3) provides deterministic, testable degradation modes for applications to handle programmatically.
acceptance_criteria: WAC prototype deployed behind runtime router in staging and can be toggled via feature flag
Per-tenant per-region token-bucket admission implemented with configurable weights and burst sizes
At least three graceful degradation modes supported: short-response truncation, model-variant fallback, tool-calling/structured-output gating
Observable metrics for admission decisions, shed rate, successful fallbacks, and SLO burn-rate exposed to Console
Canary rollback plan and automated fallback to existing global shedding if WAC misbehaves
Load test demonstrating reduced global p99 latency under identical capacity pressure compared to baseline
implementation_plan: Week 1: Spike — evaluate algorithms (weighted token bucket + priority queues) and simulate with existing load traces
Week 2: Implement admission service API (grpc) that returns {allow|degrade|reject} and metadata (reason, suggested-degradation-mode)
Week 3: Integrate admission call in routing path with minimal overhead; wire feature flag for staged rollout
Week 4: Implement degradation handlers in agent/runtime: trim max_tokens, switch to quantized model variant, disable tool calls
Week 5: Observe in staging, iterate on weighting heuristics, add per-tenant overrides and emergency operator controls
Week 6: Canary in production for subset of regions + run chaos multi-region failover test, then full rollout
tradeoffs_and_risks: Increased decision latency if admission service is synchronous — mitigate with local fast-path caches of token-bucket state
Risk of unfairness: misconfigured weights could starve smaller tenants — require sane defaults and billing-informed weights
More complex observability surfaces to correlate admission decisions to customer impact (need new Console panels)
Fallback-to-lower-fidelity models can introduce quality regressions — require automated evals and per-tenant opt-outs
testing_plan: Unit tests for admission logic and priority queue ordering
Synthetic load tests replaying peak traces with mixed tenant profiles (free, paid, reserved)
Chaos test: disable a region and observe admission behavior across remaining regions; validate SLO preservation
Regression test: validate no regression on tail latency for reserved capacity customers under normal load
monitoring_and_alerting: Shed_rate: fraction of requests that hit each degradation mode
Quality_signals: fallback_model_rate and eval-quality-regressions for canonical prompts
SLO burn-rate dashboards for p50/p95/p99 latency and availability per region and tenant tier
Operator alerts: sustained shed_rate > 5% for more than 5 minutes, or sudden spike in rejects
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged deployment to a single non-critical region (staging-like traffic) for 48h
Canary to 10% of production traffic in one region observing metrics for 72h
Expand to additional regions with progressively increasing traffic share, run chaos for each expansion
Final: enable global default but keep emergency global-circuit-breaker as backstop
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Spike completed. Two candidate algorithms evaluated: weighted token-bucket + priority lanes and proportional fair share. WEIGHTED TB chosen for deterministic behavior.
